messages:
sam.gupta: Heads up — noticed steady memory growth in KV cache during long-context sim on Dedicated (nvidia-a100 pool) vs Hosted. Hosted stabilizes ~3GB, Dedicated climbs ~7GB after ~2h. Repro attached. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

leila: Interesting. Which kernel/CUDA build on Dedicated? We saw some kernel+CUDA combos change madvise/mmap reclaim behavior before. Also did batching window change between the setups?

omar: Which perf did you run? I can grab a flame. Quick guess: slot churn + jemalloc arena contention.

sam.gupta: Dedicated nodes are Ubuntu 20.04, kernel 5.15, CUDA 11.8. Hosted is Ubuntu 22.04 + CUDA 12.1. We bumped batching window from 8->12 to hit throughput targets last month. Repro command: `./run_load --model gptx --long-context 65k --kv-enabled --runtime=dedicated`

omar: Ran `perf record -g` against the repro for 30m. Flame shows a lot in `kv_reclaim_slab` and `jemalloc` hot paths. Short dump:
```
# top stacks
kv_insert_slot 42%
kv_madvise_evict 18%
memcpy 12%
je_malloc 8%
```
Looks like eviction scanning + small allocations from batching are the heavy hitters.

rebecca: On VPC/private clusters we've observed the kernel's page reclaim latency being affected by network/storage interrupts and hugepages settings — can lead to delayed pagefree and fragmentation. Could explain hosted vs onprem differences. Quick try: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory` during a run and see if fragmentation drops. Also confirm whether we use any MAP_HUGETLB on Dedicated.

sam.gupta: Not using hugetlb. mmap flags are `MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS`, evictions call `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` for freed KV entries. On Dedicated I'm seeing madvise calls grouped and occasionally returning EAGAIN; dmesg shows anon_vma wakeups. Pasting sample dmesg lines:
`[ 13245.123] anon_vma: writeback delay, reclaim deferred`

perf-bot: perf snapshot 1850003200: [hot functions] kv_insert_slot(42%), kv_madvise_evict(18%), memcpy(12%), jemalloc_alloc(8%)

leila: Hypothesis: increasing the batch window increases transient peak KV entries per request and therefore eviction scan cost rises non-linearly. Hosted's newer kernel + CUDA appears to batch madvise/free work better (cleaner kernel thread behavior), amortizing reclaim cost. Actionable test: reduce batch window to 6 and enable a stricter prefix cache limit to see if plateau improves.

omar: I repro'd with `--batch-window=6` on Dedicated — memory plateaued around ~3.5GB instead of climbing. Also toggled `vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50` (no win) but manual `echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` temporarily reduced fragmentation. I'll run an overnight run with smaller batch and collect perf + jemalloc stats.

rebecca: For Private/on-prem, add checks for NVMe driver vs local SATA, and whether IOMMU passthrough or vfio changes page pin semantics — those can affect page reclaim. We should add a short checklist to Dedicated onboarding & troubleshooting doc so SREs can catch config drift earlier.

sam.gupta: I'll open a small perf/regression PR to add a nightly long-context KV reuse test across Hosted/Dedicated/Private that collects perf profiles, jemalloc stats, and dmesg. Assigning to myself. Thanks all :thumbsup:
